name: Mehdi Sadeghi
title: Graduate Research Associate & Ph.D. Student
affiliation: School of Sustainable Engineering and the Built Environment, Arizona State University
tagline: Developing data-driven tools and practical solutions for safer, more durable, and more sustainable pavements.
bio: I am a Graduate Research Associate and Ph.D. student in Civil Engineering at Arizona State University's School of Sustainable Engineering and the Built Environment. My work focuses on asphalt pavements and materials, pavement preservation, and airfield pavement design. I am especially interested in combining laboratory testing with programming, artificial intelligence, and data-driven modeling to help engineers make better decisions and build safer, longer-lasting, and more sustainable pavement systems.

Before joining ASU, I conducted pavement-materials research at Oklahoma State University. I enjoy turning research into useful software and practical engineering tools, and my experience also includes teaching pavement design, materials laboratories, and pavement management. I contribute to the profession as a peer reviewer for Construction and Building Materials, the International Journal of Pavement Engineering, the International Journal of Pavement Research and Technology, Road Materials and Pavement Design, and Transportation Research Record.
